items.title: Football: Moga helps Lobos control their own destiny after rallying past Cowboys 24-17
items.summary:
A new face under center brought a new pulse to New Mexico's offense on Saturday night.

New Mexico (9-2, 6-1) has won nine games in back-to-back seasons for the first time in school history and remains one win away from hosting the Mountain West championship after defeating the Wyoming Cowboys 24-17.

items.title: UNM's struggles reopen quarterback conversation ahead of pivotal game against Wyoming
items.summary:
The question of who's taking snaps under center is resurfacing in New Mexico football, again.

The question weighs more heavily than usual, thanks to last week's fourth-quarter debacle that resulted in a 21-17 loss to UNLV and ended UNM's small, but hopeful College Football Playoff chances.

items.title: Football: Cracks in offense finally shatter
items.summary:
Saturday's game started strong for the Lobos: wide receiver Bailen George threw a trick-play pass to fellow freshman wide receiver DJ Darling for a 65-yard gain on their second drive of the game, which eventually led to UNM's first touchdown of the night. All was going well.

Fast forward 10 offensive drives, and quarterback Toa Fa'avae and the Lobos' offense had managed only 40 total yards through the air, along with one touchdown pass and an interception.
